title: No Root Edit proposal reaches a token holder vote unless the Operational Facilitator first finds it aligned
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 requires that "within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment," announcing the finding on the Forum post — with reasoning attached if the finding is *misaligned*. An aligned finding must additionally "confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize."

A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 then makes the consequence explicit: "**Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment**... the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll." The vote is not a right that attaches to a submitted proposal; it is an event the Facilitator causes.

This is the load-bearing asymmetry in Pattern governance. Token holders hold the *proposal* right and the *decision* right, but a single appointed role holds a **veto that never reaches a vote**. A misalignment finding terminates the proposal without any tally, and the only remedy the text provides is the requirement to publish reasoning — reputational, not procedural.

The feasibility check compounds this: even an aligned proposal must be judged operationalizable by the Facilitator on behalf of GovOps, adding a second, more subjective ground for refusal. The design is coherent with Sky's premise that alignment must not be voteable, but it does mean Pattern's owners cannot overrule their own facilitator from inside the Artifact's routine protocol.
description: Within seven days the Facilitator must publicly rule on alignment and on GovOps feasibility; only a finding of alignment triggers the Snapshot poll, making the role a hard gate.
